design: 2 arms x 3 learning rates x 3 seeds = 18 runs. 120 steps, constant LR, 32 rollouts/step, 4096 tokens, DAPO-Math-17K. Seed varies prompt sample and training randomness. MATH500 k=4. Statistics are at the SEED level (Welch t on seed means), not the problem level.
conclusion: NULL. With three seeds per cell and seed-level statistics, v0 does not differ significantly from full-token OPD at any learning rate (p = 0.188, 0.072, 0.127), the pooled advantage is +0.0081 (p = 0.10), and the LR-robustness difference is +0.0115 with a 95% CI of [-0.0043, +0.0273] that contains zero. Both arms peak at exactly 0.7580, +0.059 over the untrained student.
what_the_single_seed_data_got_wrong: The single-seed differences were +0.0330 at 1e-5 and +0.0280 at 3e-5; with three seeds they are +0.0217 and +0.0115. Vanilla's seed 0 was unlucky at both rates and v0's was lucky. The p-values reported then (0.001, 0.002) resampled problems with the trained model held fixed, so they measured problem-sampling noise and were silent about run-to-run variance. This is exactly the failure the tutor's objection anticipated.
what_still_stands: On-policy distillation works here: +0.059 over the untrained student at 3e-6, well outside the 0.0079 seed SD.
Learning rate dominates the mask. Vanilla loses 0.039 going from 3e-6 to 3e-5 -- five times the largest arm difference measured.
v0 is never significantly worse than full-token OPD at any rate, and matches its best exactly (0.7580 vs 0.7580). A regex costing nothing does as well as training on every token.
The gradient-mass result (mass/token 0.55 for v0 against 1.48 for entropy) is a measurement, not a comparison, and is unaffected.
The teacher-forward saving ceiling of 11.6% is unaffected.
caveat: Three seeds gives a detectable difference of about 0.018 at 80% power. Effects smaller than that cannot be resolved here, and the 1e-5 p-value moved from 0.040 to 0.072 on a single added seed, so n=3 is fragile. Five or more seeds would be needed to settle differences of this size.
